answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each spun-up node requires staking collateral scaled exponentially: the first cost glows faint like an ember, but sustaining swarms compounds superlinearly, exhausting attacker capital against a solid marble ledger. Even diverse pseudonyms rooted across juniper networks fail, as validator thresholds force exponential staking penalties that render coordinated identity duplication economically ruinous.
